meta.scope: Bolivia batch 6 (final dig) — Plurinational/indigenous self-identification (Censo 2024), lithium investment contracts (China/Russia), Brazil energy relationship, and remaining trade/identity nodes. Completes deep coverage.

candidates.title: Autoidentificación indígena originaria campesina (Censo)
candidates.description: Census and survey statistics of population self-identification with Indigenous nations, peoples, or Afro-Bolivian identity. Core plurinational demographic indicator.
candidates.notes: Foundational identity node of the Plurinational State. Censo 2024: 38.7% self-identify as Indigenous or Afro-Bolivian (Quechua and Aymara the largest nations). Share has declined from 62% (2001) and 41% (2012) even as absolute numbers remain large. Continuously cited in territorial, language and rights analysis.

candidates.title: Naciones Quechua y Aymara — demographic weight
candidates.description: The two largest Indigenous nations by self-identification. Together they account for the large majority of the Indigenous population.
candidates.notes: Lived identity core of the highlands. Quechua ~1.65 m, Aymara ~1.60 m in Censo 2024. Geography overlaps heavily with the western departments and with the La Paz / El Alto metropolitan complex.

candidates.title: Territorios Indígena Originario Campesinos (TIOC)
candidates.description: Indigenous Originary Peasant Territories — recognised collective territorial units that appear as geographic domains in census and survey tabulations.
referenced_by: Poverty and service-access studies that disaggregate by TIOC
candidates.notes: Plurinational territorial node. Continuously cited as a distinct geographic and rights unit in official statistics and policy.

candidates.title: Contrato litio YLB–CBC (China)
candidates.description: Investment and service contract for direct lithium extraction and residual-brine plants in the Salar de Uyuni area, with Chinese consortium participation and majority state stake.
referenced_by: Policy debate on contract transparency and local benefit
candidates.notes: Major international industrial-investment instrument. Part of the attempt to scale lithium production from the current low base; subject to ongoing political and legislative scrutiny.

candidates.title: Contrato litio YLB–Uranium One (Rusia)
candidates.description: Investment contract for a direct lithium extraction plant with Russian partner, complementary to the Chinese CBC arrangement.
candidates.notes: Second major international lithium-investment instrument. Together with the CBC contract, defines the current external partnership architecture for lithium industrialisation.

candidates.title: Relación energética Bolivia–Brasil (gasoducto y gas)
candidates.description: Long-standing natural-gas export relationship with Brazil via the Bolivia–Brazil gas pipeline. Still the principal residual gas-export market after the end of the Argentina contract.
referenced_by: Analysis of the structural decline in gas volumes
candidates.notes: Core bilateral energy relationship. Volumes have declined but Brazil remains the main residual buyer; recent high-level statements explore ways to stabilise or expand cooperation.

candidates.title: Tasa de alfabetismo / Literacy rate
candidates.description: Literacy rate for the adult population, published nationally and by Indigenous self-identification, area and department.
candidates.notes: Long-run education-outcome indicator. National adult literacy has improved substantially (illiteracy now in the mid-single digits); gaps remain by area and by Indigenous identification.

candidates.title: Idiomas hablados / Language statistics
candidates.description: Statistics of languages spoken (Spanish, Quechua, Aymara and others), from census and household surveys. Core plurinational cultural indicator.
candidates.notes: Lived cultural node. Complements self-identification; Spanish is dominant in urban areas while Indigenous languages retain substantial weight, especially in highland and rural domains.

candidates.title: Población de 65 años y más / Population ageing
candidates.description: Share and absolute size of the population aged 65 and over. Demographic context for the Renta Dignidad and health-system pressure.
candidates.notes: Ageing signal. Share has risen (Censo 2024: ~7.4%). Links directly to the fiscal and social sustainability of the universal old-age pension.

candidates.title: Relación comercial con China
candidates.description: Bilateral trade relationship with China — major destination for minerals and origin of imports, and partner in lithium industrialisation.
candidates.notes: Structural commercial and investment partner. Continuously cited in export (minerals) and import (machinery, intermediates) analysis and in the lithium partnership architecture.

proposed_edges.basis: Indigenous self-identification is a core census question and tabulation domain.
Quechua and Aymara are the two largest nations within the self-identification totals.
TIOC appear as geographic domains in the same census identity tabulations.
The CBC contract is a principal investment instrument of YLB’s industrialisation programme.
The Uranium One contract is a principal investment instrument of YLB’s industrialisation programme.
The Brazil gas relationship structures the residual export market for Bolivian natural gas.
Literacy rates are a core long-run outcome indicator of the education system.
Language use complements self-identification as a measure of lived plurinational culture.
The size of the 65+ population is the direct demographic base of the universal old-age pension.
China is a major export destination and import origin in the merchandise-trade statistics.
